question: The political Part of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from which Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**British Constitution.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **political part** of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from the **British Constitution.**
 
• The Indian Constitution has borrowed the** parliamentary form of government, the rule of law, the bicameral legislature,** and the** office of the governor** from the British Constitution.
 
• However, the Indian Constitution has also made several modifications to the **British model** to suit the Indian context.
 
• For instance, India has a federal system of government with a strong center, while the UK has a **unitary system.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Irish Constitution** has influenced the Indian Constitution in terms of the **Directive Principles of State Policy.**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution has borrowed the idea of **social and economic justice** from the Irish Constitution. 
 
 
 
• The **Australian Constitution** has influenced the Indian Constitution in terms of the **concurrent list**, which allows both the center and the states to make laws on certain subjects.
 
• The** US Constitution** has influenced the Indian Constitution in terms of **fundamental rights**, which are similar to the** Bill of Rights** in the US Constitution.
 
 
• However, the Indian Constitution has also made several modifications to the **US model,** such as the inclusion of **socio-economic rights.**
